title: Tacos de canasta afuera del metro

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Valeria, pues tengo muchísima hambre. ¿Vamos por unos tacos de canasta aquí afuera del metro?
dialogue.english: Hey, Valeria, well I'm super hungry. Shall we get some basket tacos right outside the subway?

slang.actualMeaning: Steamed street tacos kept warm in a cloth-lined basket, often sold from a bicycle
slang.example: En la esquina del metro venden tacos de canasta buenísimos.

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ay, sí, qué rico! Pero espera, o sea, ¿traes efectivo? Porque el señor de la bicicleta no acepta tarjeta.
dialogue.english: Oh, yes, delicious! But wait, I mean, do you have cash on you? Because the guy with the bicycle doesn't take cards.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: Híjole, bueno, solo traigo un billete de cincuenta pesos en la cartera. ¿Cuánto cuesta la orden?
dialogue.english: Shoot, well, I only have a fifty-peso bill in my wallet. How much does an order cost?

slang.actualMeaning: Shoot! / Gosh! / Oh man! (classic Mexican exclamation of surprise)
slang.example: ¡Híjole, se me olvidaron las llaves adentro de la casa!

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: Pues la orden de cinco tacos sale en cuarenta pesos. Y yo tengo veinte pesos en monedas para dos refrescos.
dialogue.english: Well an order of five tacos comes to forty pesos. And I have twenty pesos in coins for two sodas.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ah, qué chido! Entonces compartimos la orden ahorita y en la tarde te paso mi parte por transferencia.
dialogue.english: Oh, awesome! Then let's share the order right now and this afternoon I'll send you my share by bank transfer.

slang.actualMeaning: How awesome / great / cool (classic Mexican slang)
slang.example: ¡Qué chido que pudiste venir a la fiesta!

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: Sale, pide dos de papa con chorizo y tres de frijol. ¡Pero aguas con la salsa verde que pica un montón!
dialogue.english: Deal, order two potato-and-chorizo ones and three bean ones. But watch out for the green salsa—it's super spicy!

slang.actualMeaning: It's super spicy / has a lot of chili heat
slang.example: No le pongas tanta salsa habanera porque pica un montón.

questions.question: What are Carlos and Valeria trying to figure out outside the subway station?
options: Whether they have enough cash to buy street tacos and sodas
Which subway line they need to take to get to a restaurant
Where to find an ATM because they lost their wallets
How to cook potato and bean tacos at home tonight
questions.explanation: Carlos is hungry for tacos de canasta outside the metro, and Valeria checks if they have enough cash since the vendor doesn't take cards.

questions.question: How much money does Carlos have on him, and how much does an order of 5 tacos cost?
options: He has a 20-peso bill, and the tacos cost 50 pesos
He has a 50-peso bill, and the 5 tacos cost 40 pesos
He has 100 pesos in coins, and the tacos cost 60 pesos
He has no cash at all, so Valeria pays 40 pesos by card
questions.explanation: Carlos says 'solo traigo un billete de cincuenta pesos' (50-peso bill), and Valeria says 'la orden de cinco tacos sale en cuarenta pesos' (40 pesos).

questions.question: Which taco fillings does Valeria ask Carlos to order for them to share?
options: Five pork tacos with red salsa
Three chicken tacos and two cheese tacos
Two potato-with-chorizo and three bean tacos
Four steak tacos and one potato taco
questions.explanation: Valeria says: 'Sale, pide dos de papa con chorizo y tres de frijol' (two potato-with-chorizo and three bean tacos).

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Carlos says 'Híjole' and '¡qué chido!', and Valeria warns the salsa 'pica un montón', what do those expressions mean?
options: 'Híjole' = shoot/oh man; 'qué chido' = how awesome; 'pica un montón' = it's super spicy
'Híjole' = hurry up; 'qué chido' = how expensive; 'pica un montón' = it costs extra
'Híjole' = excuse me; 'qué chido' = how cold; 'pica un montón' = it's sour
'Híjole' = thank you; 'qué chido' = how small; 'pica un montón' = it's very hot
questions.explanation: In Mexican Spanish, 'híjole' is 'shoot/oh man', 'qué chido' is 'how cool/awesome', and 'pica un montón' means 'it's super spicy!'
